# HEVC multi-process concurrency research

**AI disclosure:** This document, including its title and all prose, was generated by AI at the repository owner's request.

This is the research record for
[libva-v4l2_request#39](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/39).
It does **not** close the historical intermittent corruption as fixed.
Implementation remains [libva-v4l2_request#43](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/43) (H4).

## Problem

Historical four-process HEVC runs sometimes mismatched `SLIST_B_Sony_9`,
`SLIST_D_Sony_9` or `RAP_B_Bossen_2` without an AVD firmware error. Serial
results on this machine are 144/147 (the three known serial failures). Three
later clean four-process suites at r9 are useful but did not capture a
reproducer.

Kernel patch 0006 (read HEVC controls after applying the request so a
queued-ahead next picture cannot change the current picture's slice count) is
already in the omarchy-m1-video patchset. This campaign looks for **remaining
pixel mismatches**, not that control race.

## Harness

`tests/hevc-concurrent.py` starts N processes behind a barrier, each running
`tests/frame-check.c` through VA-API. It must be wrapped by `tests/hwguard.py`.
`--seed` and `--schedule` are recorded. The first hash mismatch stops the
schedule. Software references are checked first.

```sh
python3 tests/hwguard.py --journal-since '2026-09-16 00:00:00' --deadline 600 -- \
  python3 tests/hevc-concurrent.py --driver build/src \
    --resources /path/to/JCT-VC-HEVC_V1 --frame-check ./frame-check \
    --schedule four-named --repeat 5 --seed 39-four-named --output /path/to/out
```

`--journal-since` is required on this boot because 2026-09-15 16:33 PDT left
`H3 error` / `Frame processing timed out!` in the kernel log. New faults after
the since-stamp still abort.

|---|---|
| Machine | Apple M1 T8103, `/dev/video0`, idle before/after |
| Userspace | `avd-fixes` `826d175`, unsanitized `build-conc/src` |
| Software refs | All four named vectors match Fluster MD5s |
| Seed prefix | `39-<schedule>` |
| Named MD5s | SLIST_B `312b4ebb3e885587d5e12b78aa95977a`; SLIST_D `8d38ce43b17627ff1f86e526bfb7ffc4`; RAP_B `f38befcc280f2fd0d23f48f807f843c2`; RAP_A `8a536a80ed42b37b1ac5810bc046f82a` |
| Wall clock | 2026-09-16T00:05:13-0700 – 00:06:27-0700 (**74 s**), deadline 600 s; slot `elapsed_s` ≈ 0.4 s |
| Result | **23/23 runs matched**, 0 pixel mismatches, 0 new AVD faults |

| Schedule | Repeats | Processes | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `pair-bd` SLIST_B + SLIST_D | 5 | 2 | 5/5 match |
| `pair-br` SLIST_B + RAP_B | 5 | 2 | 5/5 match |
| `pair-dr` SLIST_D + RAP_B | 5 | 2 | 5/5 match |
| `four-named` B+D+RAP_B+RAP_A | 5 | 4 | 5/5 match |
| `four-slist-b` four SLIST_B | 3 | 4 | 3/3 match |

Pinned slot hashes: `tests/fixtures/hevc-concurrency/campaign.json`.

One earlier `pair-br` attempt aborted as `foreign-client` because multiprocessing
workers were not treated as descendants of the guard child. That is a guard
ownership bug, not HEVC corruption. Ancestry walking was added; the schedule
was rerun clean.

## Layer / 0006

No pixel mismatch was captured, so this campaign cannot name a remaining
userspace or firmware invariant. It also cannot attribute historical failures
to 0006 (already applied) or to Chrome holding the decoder (no extra clients
during these runs).

## H4 contract

- A clean schedule does **not** close H3/H4.
- 23/23 on four named vectors in 74 s does **not** bound the historical 147-vector
  four-process fault. Next experiment: longer four-process full `JCT-VC-HEVC_V1`
  (147 vectors), or the same pairs with an extra unrelated decoder client, or
  more than five repeats. Stop on the first wrong hash and keep that run's frame logs.
- Do not land a “fix” without a captured mismatch and first differing frame.

## Tests not run

- Full 147-vector four-process suite
- Chrome or mpv as a third decoder client
- Module reload / reboot (stale 2026-09-15 journal lines remain)
- Kernel traces
